$comment: Assessment-surface map: every normative (MUST / MUST NOT / REQUIRED / forbidden, plus the imperative verifier contract of §7) statement of docs/specs/aep-profile-v1.md, mapped to the verifier check that executes it (lib/src/check-registry.ts) or to 'no-executable-check' when no code in the TypeScript verifier executes it. This file is the DENOMINATOR for any 'share of the spec assessed' figure: it is derived from the spec surface, not from the verifier's own check list, and lib/test/assessment-surface.test.ts two-set-diffs it against CHECK_REGISTRY so neither side can drift silently. Edit it only together with the spec or the registry. OVERT is an open standard published by Glacis Technologies, Inc. (https://overt.is); this project is independent of Glacis Technologies, carries no endorsement or certification by them, and the overt_receipt.json clauses below describe an OVERT-inspired entry that is not claimed to be OVERT-conformant.

clauses.statement: A v1 .aep package is a ZIP archive (PKZIP, store or deflate).
The archive is a flat directory of named files; nested directories are forbidden in v1.
Maximum uncompressed size: 10 MB.
Every v1 package MUST include response.txt, canonical.bin, hash.sha256, signature.sig, public_key.pem, metadata.json, timestamp.tsr with these exact names.
response.txt is UTF-8 text, no BOM, line endings preserved as-issued.
hash.sha256 is the lower-case hex SHA-256 of canonical.bin.
signature.sig is the Base64 PKCS#1 v1.5 RSA signature over canonical.bin (inner digest SHA-256), verifiable against public_key.pem.

The same §3 signature obligation, executed a second way: signatures Web Crypto refuses are re-checked against the raw DigestInfo encoding for Java reference compatibility. The fallback mechanism itself is a verifier implementation detail, not a spec sentence.
metadata.json is machine-readable UTF-8 JSON.

metadata.json is 'canonicalised per section 4.4' (a dangling reference — the JSON canonicalisation rules live in §6 step 2). Neither verifier checks that the stored entry bytes are in canonical JSON form, and the TypeScript signer writes non-canonical JSON.stringify output.
When PQC entries are present, the ML-DSA-65 signature over canonical.bin verifies against pqc_public_key.pem.

When the issuing TSP is configured to emit post-quantum signatures, the PQC entries MUST be present. The verifier cannot observe the issuer's configuration, so absence is never distinguishable from a pre-Phase-1.9 deployment.

Verifiers that process overt_receipt.json MUST reject the package if the receipt is present and inconsistent: overt MUST equal 1.0.0; profile MUST equal urn:eatf:spec:aep:1.0; scope MUST be non-empty; subject.agent_id / subject.tenant_hash / event.timestamp / event.action_type / policy.version / policy.coverage / policy.decision MUST match their metadata.json counterparts when present; content_hash MUST equal sha256:<hash.sha256>; witness.signature_refs MUST be a non-empty array of flat filenames that exist non-empty in the package; witness.timestamp_refs MUST be an array of such filenames; unknown receipt fields MUST be ignored.
profile_revision MUST identify the AEP draft/release that generated the receipt. Not checked by either verifier.
subject.tenant_hash MUST NOT contain a raw tenant id. Undecidable from package contents alone.
witness.iap MUST identify the independent attestation provider. The verifier checks the refs arrays but never the iap field.

metadata.json MUST carry a warrant_digest equal to the lower-case hex SHA-256 of warrant.json as packaged; a warrant.json without that reference, a reference without the entry, or a digest mismatch is inconsistent and MUST be rejected.

The packaged warrant bytes MUST be the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form of a record with the required fields of schemas/warrant-v1.schema.json (warrant_id, warrant_version, policy_ref, inference_form, statement, applies_to, valid_from, valid_until) and a machine/attested-partitioned void_if when present.

The warrant is bound through metadata.json, so the binding holds only under the profile canonical form of section 6; under the response-only compatibility form the verifier MUST report the warrant as unbound.
policy_ref.policy_id / policy_ref.policy_version MUST equal metadata.json policy_id / policy_version, and metadata warrant_id / warrant_version MUST match the record when present.
A metadata action_type or policy_decision outside applies_to is reported — the output may inform but carries no warrant to compel — and MUST NOT by itself fail verification.
acceptance.signature MUST verify as a PKCS#1 v1.5 RSA signature (inner digest SHA-256) over the JCS bytes of the warrant with acceptance.signature removed, against acceptance.public_key.

An RFC 3161 genTime outside valid_from..valid_until is reported and MUST NOT by itself fail verification. A genTime inside the window supports a fresh verdict only when the timestamp chains to a trusted root (the tsa-chain-to-root tri-state), so the affirmative outcome needs a caller-supplied trust list.
The soundness of the licensed inference and the key-to-principal binding of the accepting authority are attested, never machine-checked. Attested-only.
void_if entries of kind 'attested' carry text a human must attest to; entries of kind 'machine' carry predicates the v0.1 verifiers record but do not evaluate. Attested-only in this release.

When metadata.json carries an accepting_authority block, the acceptance is bound to this output only under the profile canonical form; a detached acceptance.json, when packaged, MUST match accepting_authority.acceptance_digest (sha256 of its JCS bytes) and its principal / policy_id / policy_version MUST agree. Under the response-only compatibility form the whole block is unsigned and the acceptance is unbound. GATES: an acceptance that is not bound to this output makes verification FAIL.

When a detached acceptance.json is packaged, acceptance.sig MUST verify as a PKCS#1 v1.5 RSA signature (inner digest SHA-256) over the JCS bytes of acceptance.json against its embedded public_key. Key binding is reported separately from role. GATES: a packaged acceptance whose signature does not verify makes verification FAIL.

The RFC 3161 genTime is checked for containment in accepting_authority.validity (not_before..not_after). A genTime outside the window is reported and MUST NOT by itself fail verification. This imports AdES temporal-validation semantics (ETSI EN 319 102-1, TS 119 615), never invented.

Role assertion of the accepting authority is attested-only unless the caller supplies an authorityTrustList, mirroring the tsa-chain-to-root tri-state: when supplied, the accepting authority's public key is checked for membership and the result is reported separately from key binding.

The key-to-principal binding of the accepting authority is attested, never machine-checked (the same self-attestation trust model as public_key.pem); nothing in the profile establishes the accepting authority as a legally constituted authority. Attested-only.

When metadata.json carries a voiding array, the verifier evaluates every typed predicate at verify time against caller-supplied inputs (a dated registry snapshot, a supersession list) — never a network fetch — and emits a four-valued verdict per entry (holds / voided / unknown / not-assessed). For registry-status predicates the same snapshot is read at the RFC 3161 genTime and at the snapshot instant and the verdict PAIR is surfaced, never collapsed (imported AdES / eIDAS dual-time semantics, ETSI EN 319 102-1 / TS 119 615, polarity inverted). An unknown predicate type MUST yield not-assessed, never holds. Informational in this release; a voided verdict does not by itself fail verification.

Voiding predicates of type 'attested', and predicates whose caller-supplied input is absent, are reported as not-assessed / unknown respectively; they are not machine-decided from package bytes alone. Attested-only / input-dependent.

When metadata.json carries an authorizing_principal block that names a principal and nothing else, no signed mandate is claimed and the verifier MUST report every mandate check as not determinate rather than as a pass. When the block carries mandate_digest, or the package carries a mandate.json entry, a signed mandate is claimed: mandate_digest MUST equal 'sha256:' plus the lower-case hex SHA-256 of mandate.json as packaged, and a reference without the entry, an entry without the reference, or a mismatch MUST be rejected.

The packaged mandate bytes MUST be the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form of a record with the required fields of schemas/mandate-v1.schema.json (mandate_id, mandate_version, principal, subject, granted_at, statement, scope, valid_from, valid_until, public_key).

A claimed mandate MUST be bound to the bytes signature.sig covers: the package MUST use the profile canonical form of section 6, and the record's mandate_id / principal / subject MUST equal the signed metadata's authorizing_principal.mandate_ref / authorizing_principal.principal / agent_id. A mandate carried under the response-only compatibility form MUST be rejected — deliberately stricter than the corresponding obligations of sections 4.2 and 4.3, which report and accept.

mandate.sig MUST verify as a PKCS#1 v1.5 RSA signature (inner digest SHA-256) over the JCS bytes of mandate.json, against the record's embedded public_key. A package cannot assert a mandate its named granting authority never signed, and a failure MUST be rejected.
A metadata action_type or policy_id outside scope.action_types / scope.policy_ids is reported — the output may inform but carries no mandate to compel — and MUST NOT by itself fail verification.
The RFC 3161 genTime is checked for containment in the mandate's valid_from..valid_until. A genTime outside the window is reported and MUST NOT by itself fail verification.

The key-to-principal binding of the granting authority is attested, never machine-checked (the same self-attestation trust model as public_key.pem), and whether the grant the mandate makes is lawful is attested, never machine-checked. Attested-only.

Fields are REQUIRED unless explicitly optional. The TypeScript verifier only parses metadata.json; required-field presence is validated nowhere at verify time (schemas/aep-v1.schema.json covers it in CI over the test vectors only, and requires only created_at).
Implementations MUST ignore unknown metadata fields (forward compatibility). Satisfied by construction: the verifier reads only the fields it cross-checks.

Verifiers MUST accept both the tenant-bound and the legacy urn:uuid form; new registrations MUST emit the tenant-bound form. The verifier never validates agent_id shape, so acceptance is trivial and the producer-side rule is unobservable.

canonical.bin is response.txt + LF + JCS(metadata.json), implementations MUST NOT include any other entries in the canonical bytes, and a verifier MUST refuse a package whose recomputed canonical bytes do not match the embedded canonical.bin.

The reference verifiers additionally accept the legacy response-only form (canonical.bin equals response.txt verbatim) and report which form matched; relying parties that depend on signed metadata MUST check for the profile form.
Implementations that normalise response.txt line endings MUST do it before building the package and document the rule in metadata.canonicalisation. Producer-side; unobservable at verify time.
timestamp.tsr decodes from Base64 and parses as an RFC 3161 TimeStampToken (contract items 1-2).
messageImprint.hashAlgorithm is SHA-256 and messageImprint.hashedMessage equals the SHA-256 of the ASCII hash.sha256 hex string (contract items 3-4).
The TSA's signature verifies using the certificate carried in the token (contract item 5, in-token half).

The TSA's certificate is validated against an out-of-band trust list (contract item 5, out-of-band half). Informational in v0.1: issuer-DN match against pinned roots, not full RFC 5280 path validation.

EATF signing certificates conform to RFC 5280 with the stated algorithm, subject CN, validity, and EKU rules. The package carries a bare public key, never a signer certificate, so no verifier can execute this clause.

When the caller supplies a non-empty trusted-signer list, the verifier MUST check public_key.pem for membership (ignoring PEM whitespace) and MUST reject a package whose signing key is not a member. When no list is supplied the check is not assessed and the issuer is attested only — the default self-attestation trust model.

Without a caller-supplied trusted-signer list, a package re-authored end to end under a different key (canonical bytes, hash, signature and public key all recomputed) is indistinguishable from a package of the expected issuer by any other obligation in this profile. Attested-only.
Existing verifiers MUST still accept packages after a minor (additive) profile bump. A behavioural obligation on future verifier releases, not a per-package check.

A v1-conformant verifier MUST produce expected results on every vector (accept every valid/ vector, reject every invalid/ vector). Met by the CI conformance jobs, not by a check inside a single verification run.
